Theme 002 · Product UI as the stage

⌘K Keyboard Symphony

The product dims and blurs behind one oversized command palette; the typed query is the headline and chunky 3D keycaps get struck on the kick drum. Acme Pulse lives inside the palette, so finding the anomaly and deciding what to do are the same two keystrokes.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Palette modal — search field + result list; the whole stage.
  • 3D keycap HUD — ⌘ K, ↵, ⌥ R keys that physically press on the beat.
  • Fuzzy-match highlight — matched letters in coral as the query types.
  • Scope chip — “Pulse ›” shows we are now inside the agent.
  • Result row with shortcut hint — right-aligned ⌥ R / ⌥ A keys; the selected row carries a teal bar.
  • Half-visible last row — faded row that hints there is always more (+33).

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Beat-typed query — one character per 1/8 note (0.25 s at 120 BPM), caret blink 530 ms between phrases.
  • Result re-rank — rows swap places with FLIP, 0.25 s power3.out; the new top row lands exactly on a beat.
  • Keycap press — translateY 10 px + shadow collapse in 80 ms on the kick, spring release (elastic.out 1, 0.5) 0.2 s later.

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Why: the command palette is the most recognisable “power user” gesture in modern software, and it makes human control literal: the anomaly only goes away when a key is pressed. Readable at feed size because it is one centred box. Risk: reads developer-only; soften with plain-language result rows and keep the typed query short.

Adapt to your product: replace the result rows with your own objects and actions, and let your product's name be the scope chip; the final ↵ is always your CTA.
